arjun: Heads-up: found a weird behavior with the console's cohort-weighted overrides. Preview shows expected routing weights, but after apply a subset of tenants end up with the parent's default weight instead of the override.
tara: repro steps?
arjun: Exported scope=cohort, added weighted override for cohort 'beta' with weights `{"routeA": 80, "routeB": 20}`. Console preview shows those numbers per-tenant. After apply some tenants still report `routeA: 50, routeB: 50` (org default).
migs: Did you use the new "apply in batches" checkbox? That does partial commits currently.
arjun: I did. But this repro also happens when "apply atomically" is selected. Seems nondeterministic across ~7% of tenants.
dev-qa: Can you paste the minimal payload you sent?
arjun: payload (redacted):
```
{ "scope": "cohort", "cohort_id": "beta", "overrides": [{"tenant_id":"t-1","weights": {"routeA":80,"routeB":20}}, {"tenant_id":"t-2","weights": {"routeA":80,"routeB":20}}] }
```
ndev-qa: Hmm console builds a merge map client-side. If server merge expects `overrides_map` keyed by tenant_id, list->map conversion is done server-side. Could be a race w/ streaming reconcile job.
tara: ops-bot, any config service deploys around 1718702500?
ops-bot: deploy:config-api v4.3.1 at 1718702480 by ci-pipeline (note: background-reconciler enabled).
migs: background reconcilers aggressive mode can stomp pending applies if versioning not honored. Maybe reconcile read sees partially-applied state and rewrites with default.
arjun: That'd explain randomness. If apply writes tenant-by-tenant and reconciler treats missing weights as default, we race.
tara: Proposed fix: server should compute a merged final-state in-memory (dry-run) and publish via atomic namespace swap (versioned key). Reconciler should prefer latest versioned namespace.
migs: Less invasive: add a per-apply generation id on the namespace + reconciler check that refuses to reconcile keys with newer generation. If reconcile sees generation < latest, skip.
dev-qa: Add server endpoint `/v1/config/merge-preview` that accepts the same payload and returns the computed final-state map without committing. Console can call that post-apply-preview to show the server view.
arjun: Love that. Also we should make apply operations single RPC with a 'commit' step so reconcile doesn't see half-done writes. Atomic swap is ideal (write new ns, flip pointer).
tara: UX: console should visually indicate when reconcile is active and warn that background reconciliation could temporarily change values. Also show "last-applied-generation" per-cohort.
migs: For safety, make default semantics `mode=replace` in UI but allow `mode=merge` with explicit warning. Also require `If-Match` header on replace to avoid lost-update.
dev-qa: Telemetry suggestions: emit `config.apply.request`, `config.apply.preview_server_hash`, `config.apply.commit_generation`, `config.apply.reconcile_conflict`. Include fields: `tenants_touched`, `mode`, `sampled_payload_size`. Full payload sampling 0.5%, metadata 100%.
arjun: Also we need a defensive server-side validate: reject input shapes that mix list/map or have missing weights. Return 4xx with structured error listing offending tenant_ids.
tara: Rollout plan: patch reconciler to be generation-aware in canary; roll server merge-preview + atomic-swap in staging; enable console server-preview flag behind `config.apply.server_preview` and run e2e on 200 tenants.
migs: For rollback strategy, keep previous namespace around for N minutes and expose `revert` API that flips pointer back. That makes reverts cheap.
dev-qa: I'll write the flaky e2e that simulates reconciler running concurrently with apply.
arjun: I'll open the issue and PR with failing trace and sample tenants. Tagging @migs and @dev-qa for pair debugging.
ops-bot: incident:cohort-weighted-mismatch created at 1718702690 (investigating).
tara: Thanks team. Let's aim for staging fix by tomorrow and notify support to hold further bulk cohort-imports in staging until then.
migs: I'll prototype generation tagging today.
darjun: (typo fix) will paste logs in PR.
